agnostic.prompt: Audit the entire repository for compliance with all applicable instructions in the currently applicable AGENTS.md files. Present all findings in a (possibly giant) enumerated list. For each item, include a file/line reference, an explanation of the exact nature of the violation or lacking compliance, and a recommended action.

agnostic.gloss: Ensure ASCII-only source files wherever possible
agnostic.prompt: Audit the current repository and enforce ASCII-only source code and configuration wherever possible. Allow non-ASCII characters for example in documentation files when a literal Unicode character is genuinely necessary or seems intentionally desired. Replace avoidable non-ASCII characters with ASCII equivalents or suitable totally equivalent escape codes. Add, update, or confirm the presence of automated checks to prevent regressions. Strictly preserve all existing code behavior.

agnostic.gloss: Enumerate all kinds of discernible TODOs in a repo
agnostic.prompt:
Scan the entire repository for unfinished, temporary, obsolete, or cleanup-related work. Look for all kinds of todos, like:

- Explicit markers such as TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, TBD, and similar annotations
- Unfinished or placeholder code
- Commented-out or dead code
- Temporary debugging logic, logging, prints, flags, or test hooks
- Stub implementations, dummy values, hard-coded temporary values, and unimplemented branches
- Documentation that describes incomplete, planned, or unresolved work
- Obsolete, duplicate, backup, generated, or accidentally committed files
- Temporary artifacts that are tracked but should likely be ignored
- Empty, unused, or suspicious files and directories
- References to files, modules, commands, configuration, or features that no longer exist
- Deprecated compatibility code that may no longer be needed
- Any other repository content that appears to have been left behind unintentionally or still requires follow-up work

Avoid reporting findings for things that are clearly part of legitimate user-facing content, test data, vendored dependencies, generated files, or historical documentation. Use repository-wide search, version-control metadata, language-aware static analysis, file-type inspection, and other mechanistic approaches where useful. Do not limit the search to source-code comments. Present all findings in a (possibly giant) enumerated list. For each item, include a file/line reference, a full statement of the todo, and a brief explanation why it has been considered a todo.

agnostic.gloss: Execute a markdown implementation plan in goal mode

prompt_vars.%MarkdownPlanFile%: Markdown file containing details of the plan to implement.

agnostic.prompt: Implement the comprehensive implementation plan in %MarkdownPlanFile% completely and correctly. First read the entire plan file and all directly referenced project guidance needed to understand it; treat the plan file as the authoritative implementation specification. Implement every task, milestone, acceptance criterion, migration note, required test, documentation update, cleanup item, and verification step described there, preserving existing behavior unless the plan explicitly requires a change. Work in audited checkpoints: inspect the relevant code, make cohesive changes, update or add required tests/docs, run the most relevant available verification commands, fix failures caused by your changes, and keep a compact progress log of what changed, what was verified, and what remains. The goal is complete ONLY when every in-scope plan item is implemented, every acceptance criterion in the plan is satisfied, all relevant verification passes or any remaining failure is proven unrelated to the changes, and the final response lists changed files plus exact verification commands and results. HARD BLOCKING RULE: if at any point there is any doubt, unclarity, ambiguity, conflict, missing context, required user decision/input, required manual user action, unavailable credential/secret, unsafe/destructive operation, unclear product behavior, unclear scope boundary, or any other situation where proceeding would require guessing, Codex MUST immediately **block the goal**, ask specific enumerated questions or request the exact user action needed, and then **immediately end its turn** in a blocked goal state so that the user can respond; Codex MUST NOT continue, MUST NOT guess, MUST NOT simulate waiting, MUST NOT poll for a response, and MUST NOT ask the same question repeatedly in a loop: after asking once, it must wait for new user input before proceeding.
agnostic.notes: If the goal stops to ask questions, answer them in a new prompt and append to the prompt: Do not do anything other than respond to this with 'Acknowledge'. Only once the acknowledgement comes back resume the goal with a second prompt: /goal resume

agnostic.gloss: Identify trivial wrapper functions across the codebase
agnostic.prompt:
Scan the entire codebase for functions or methods that appear to be trivial wrappers: very short implementations that do little more than forward arguments, call another function, return a very short/simple single expression, or perform similarly minimal work. Use language-appropriate static analysis, AST tooling, repository search, or other mechanistic techniques to identify candidates efficiently rather than relying only on manual inspection. For each candidate, produce a finding containing:

- The function/method name and location
- Its complete implementation as a well-formatted code block
- The number of call sites
- A brief explanation of why it is or is not a good candidate for removal
- Any relevant reasons to preserve it, such as abstraction boundaries, API stability, naming value, instrumentation, validation, compatibility, overriding, mocking, or future extensibility
- A recommended action: inline and remove, keep, or investigate further

When recommending removal, verify that the wrapper can be safely inlined at every call site without changing behavior, visibility, dispatch, error handling, typing, evaluation order, or public API compatibility.
